Synopsis:
The Indian rupee fell 0.3% to 95.44/USD, its third consecutive daily loss, driven by surging oil prices (+6% on the week), elevated dollar demand from derivatives expiry and corporate hedging. RBI intervention via state-run banks continued but at a reduced scale versus the prior week's ~$8B deployment. The RBI also conducted sell/buy FX swaps for a second straight day to drain INR liquidity, pushing 1-year forward premiums to 3.37% — a multi-month high. Broader FX markets were largely range-bound ahead of ECB rate decision and the next day's US CPI print, both seen as pivotal near-term catalysts.
